title: HTTP Lifecycle Request Artifact Adapter
summary: The FP-MCP-255 read-only HTTP lifecycle request adapter was implemented, exposed, and verified. A fresh non-executing request artifact was recorded for FP-MCP-254 with modelId=deepseek-v4-pro-high and runMode=DESIGN_ONLY, producing requestId REQ-20260703T231957999Z-32fcb25f. The request artifact was committed as supporting evidence at ForgePilot commit 7b9ba35. The adapter then read that request artifact, validated request identity, requested model, requested run mode, CREATED_NOT_STARTED state, and bounded prompt policy, and returned lifecyclePlanReady=true. The adapter bound promptText=Return exactly: OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK and expectedText=OPENCODE_HTTP_CANARY_OK by SHA-256, returned lifecycleToolName=forgepilot_run_opencode_http_lifecycle_orchestrator, lifecycleApprovalRequired=RUN_OPENCODE_HTTP_LIFECYCLE_ORCHESTRATOR, lifecycleCleanupDefault=true, and confirmed executionAuthorized=false, approvalConsumed=false, runnerStartEndpointContacted=false, opencodeStarted=false, and lifecycleInvoked=false.
caveats: The adapter is plan-only and does not invoke the lifecycle orchestrator.
The request artifact used for verification was intentionally created as non-executing evidence for this adapter test.
The adapter binds prompt and expected text by hash but does not persist a separate lifecycle plan artifact yet.
The current request artifact schema does not carry prompt text itself, so bounded promptText and expectedText are adapter inputs.
boundaries: No OpenCode session was created by the adapter.
No prompt was submitted by the adapter.
No wait endpoint was called by the adapter.
No session was deleted by the adapter.
No OpenCode process was started by the adapter.
No runner start endpoint was contacted by the adapter.
No approval was consumed by the adapter.
No lifecycle was invoked by the adapter.
